📖 Core Definitions

Essential Terminology & Concepts

Fuzzy Singleton Core Definition

Fuzzy Singleton a fuzzy set in which there is exactly one element which has positive membership value.

Fuzzy Systems Key Concept

In the symbolic Logic systems like, PL and FOPL, that we have studied so far, any (closed) formula has a truth-value which must be binary, viz., True or False.

Fuzzy Set Representation Key Concept

(ii) A ∩ B is the largest subset of X contained in both A and B.

Fuzzy Reasoning Key Concept

When some axiom is added to a PL or an FOPL system, then, through deduction, we can draw more conclusions.

Fuzzy Inference Key Concept

PL and FOPL are deductive inferencing systems: i.e., the conclusions drawn are invariably true whenever the premises are true.

📌 Key Takeaways

Section-by-Section Study Breakdown

8.2 Fuzzy Systems

  • In the symbolic Logic systems like, PL and FOPL, that we have studied so far, any (closed) formula has a truth-value which must be binary, viz., True or False.
  • However, in our everyday experience, we encounter problems, the descriptions of which involve some words, because of which, to statements of situations, it is not possible to assign a truth value: True or False.
  • Some other cases of Fuzziness in a Natural Language Healthy Person: we cannot even enumerate all the parameters that determine health.
  • Further, it is even more difficult to tell for what value of a particular parameter, one is healthy or otherwise.

8.4 Fuzzy Set Representation

  • (ii) A ∩ B is the largest subset of X contained in both A and B.
  • (iii) The complement A' is such that (a) A and A' do not have any element in common and (b) Every element of the universal set is in either A or A'.
  • Thus, smaller the value of degree of membership, a sort of lesser it is a member of the Fuzzy set.
  • (2) While taking union of Crisp sets, members of both sets are included, and none else.

8.5 Fuzzy Reasoning

  • When some axiom is added to a PL or an FOPL system, then, through deduction, we can draw more conclusions.
  • Hence, more additional facts become available in the knowledge base with the addition of each axiom.
  • Adding of axioms to the knowledge base increases the amount of knowledge contained in the knowledge base.
  • Therefore, the set of facts through inferences in such systems can only grow larger with addition of each axiomatic fact.

8.6 Fuzzy Inference

  • PL and FOPL are deductive inferencing systems: i.e., the conclusions drawn are invariably true whenever the premises are true.
  • However, due to limitations of these systems for making inferences, as discussed earlier, we must have other systems inferences.
  • The abductive inference is useful in diagnostic applications.
  • For example while diagnosing a disease (say P), the doctor asks for the symptoms (say Q).

8.7 Rough Set Theory

  • Rough set theory can be regarded as a new mathematical tool for imperfect data analysis.
  • The theory has found applications in many domains, such as decision support, engineering, environment, banking, medicine and others.
  • It is a mechanism to deal with imprecise/imprecise knowledge, dealing with such a kind of knowledge is particularly area of research for the scientists, working in the field of Artificial Intelligence.
  • There are various approaches to handle the imprecise knowledge, the most successful one is that of the Fuzzy logic, which was proposed by L.Zadeh, we discussed the same in our earlier sections of this unit.
